notes.meaning: A father urges his child to hold onto wise teachings and store them up like hidden treasure. When God's instructions are kept close, they protect us from making foolish choices.
Obeying God's rules brings true life and lasting well-being. A person should protect God's teachings as carefully as they protect the pupil of their eye, which is tender and precious.
God's truth should be as close and ready as a ring on a finger. It must not just stay on a scroll, but be deeply settled into a person's inner thoughts and affections.
We are called to love wisdom like a dear family member. Treating God's understanding as a close, beloved sister helps guard our hearts against evil desires.
Deep love for God's wisdom serves as a shield against unfaithfulness. It reveals the danger hidden behind the flattering and smooth talk of a temptress.

other.label: Modern scholarship
other.view: Some scholars suggest that the 'strange woman' could refer historically to foreign wives or worshippers of other gods after the return from the Babylonian exile.

notes.meaning: The teacher describes looking out through the wooden slats of his window to watch what happens in the street. This story shows in plain terms how easily an unwary person can be tricked.
Among the crowd, the speaker spots an inexperienced young man who lacks good sense. He is not necessarily set in evil ways yet, but his lack of judgment makes him an easy target for danger.
The idle young man wanders near the street corner where an immoral woman is known to linger. Instead of staying far away, he puts himself directly in the path of temptation.
He hangs around outside as evening fades into pitch-black night. People who look for wrongdoing often wait for darkness to hide what they are doing from others.
A married woman steps out into the street dressed like a prostitute to catch his attention. Beneath her bold appearance lies a guarded, calculating mind looking to satisfy her own desires.
This woman refuses to stay quietly at home and rejects proper boundaries. She roams the busy public streets and waits at corners to hunt for someone to seduce.
She grabs the young man without hesitation and kisses him in public. Showing no shame or respect for God's law, she looks him in the face and begins to entice him.
She claims that she just completed her religious thank-offerings and has sacred food ready to eat at home. She uses a show of religion as a cover for sin, inviting him over to share the feast.

other.label: Modern scholarship
other.view: Some scholars propose that her religious vows were linked to ancient pagan fertility rituals rather than ordinary Israelite sacrifices.

notes.meaning: She flatters the young man by pretending she came outside just to look for him. This false praise feeds his pride and makes him feel uniquely special.
She describes her couch dressed in expensive, imported Egyptian linens and perfumed with sweet-smelling spices. Every detail is designed to excite his senses and draw him into her bedroom.
She urges him to spend the entire night with her indulging in physical pleasure. She calls this stolen passion 'love,' even though it is sinful and will lead to ruin.
She assures the young man that her husband is far away on business and will not be back until the full moon. By promising that there is no chance of being caught, she removes his fear of discovery.
Her constant, smooth talking wears down his remaining hesitation. Her deceptive words overcome his conscience and pull him away from what is right.
The young man follows her without thinking, just like an animal walking calmly toward death. He only notices the immediate bait, blind to the fact that this choice will destroy his life.
The teacher turns to address all young learners directly after telling this cautionary tale. He urges them to pay close attention so they do not fall into the same trap.
A person must guard their very first thoughts from wandering toward an immoral life. Staying away begins on the inside, by refusing to desire or wander down dangerous paths.
Sinful lust has destroyed countless victims throughout history, including strong and capable men. No one is naturally tough or clever enough to play with sexual sin and escape unharmed.
Walking into the temptress's home is like taking a direct highway to the grave and the place of destruction. What begins as a search for pleasure ends in spiritual and physical ruin.
